about: The one spec the three gates share: audit_design.py, stylelint.config.mjs and eslint.design.config.mjs. tools/sync_rules.py writes its data (the layer order, the nesting depth, the system colours, the value shapes and allowlists, the colour functions, the theme bindings, the geometry properties) into a marked block in each gate, and its --check fails when a block drifts from this file. Each section's `gates` names the tools that enforce it, and the conformance tests (tests/test_rules_spec.py, tests/test_real_tools.py) run every `allowed` and `refused` example through each of them. Change a rule here first, rerun the tool, then change whatever gate code the data cannot express. Source of the rules: token-contract.md, the Nine Laws.

nesting.counts: Nested style rules below the top-level rule. @media, @supports, @layer, @container and @scope do not count, and neither does a rule whose selector is only pseudo-classes (`:hover`, as opposed to `&:hover`).

selectors.rule: Law 5: a selector says what an element is; layers decide who wins. Its specificity stays at or under 0,3,1, compared column by column: three classes, attributes or pseudo-classes, and one element. `:where()` scores zero, `:is()`, `:not()` and `:has()` score their heaviest argument, and a nested rule's `&` scores its parent's, as Selectors 4 says. A selector holds at most three compound selectors, counted as written, inside a functional pseudo-class too: `:where()` takes away the weight, not the knowledge of the DOM. stylelint 17 also counts the `+` of an An+B (`:nth-last-child(n + 5)`), so a quantity query carries its disable comment there. An id is refused on its own.

zero.rule: A literal 0 is allowed wherever a length token is. --space-0 exists for token files and layout primitives; component code writes 0.

tiers.rule: Law 6: component code reads roles. Reading a Tier-1 primitive that has a role (with_role, by prefix, with the advice the audit gives) skips a tier. Not leaks: the page-rhythm roles that live under --space- (tier2_exceptions), and the null-outs, which assert no value (nulls). design-system-docs' extract_system.py reads the same three lists for its tier1-leak gap, so the two agree.

with_role.leading-: a type role (--type-*), which carries leading in its shorthand

margins_in_components.rule: Law 2: a component never sets its own outer margin. Legal: alignment, 0s and autos only (`0 auto`, `0 0 0 auto`), calc(var(--token) * -1) to cancel a known token, the owl, the whole `> * + *` in the parent's own rule, through any @media around the margin, and a margin on the component's own generated content (::before, ::after, ::marker), which sits inside it. `.card + *` is not the owl: it is the component spacing its next sibling. `var(--gap-related) auto` is not alignment: the token sets the component's own block margin. A selector that names `prose` is no exemption: a `.prose` flow container is a layout, and belongs in a layout file, where its owl is allowed anyway.

geometry.rule: A position is geometry, not a step of a scale: `calc((var(--tap-min) - 100%) / -2)` centres a hit area on its box, and a percentage, a factor of a token, or an em (sup and sub ride on their text) is how geometry is written. So the audit refuses only a literal length that is not an em, and stylelint has no allowlist for these properties, because no shape can name every correct calc(). The audit reads the list from GEOMETRY_PROPERTIES.

var_fallback.rule: A var() fallback is not checked: the token is the value, and the fallback only renders when the token is missing.

system_colors.rule: A CSS system colour (Canvas, ButtonText, Highlight and the rest) is correct only inside @media (forced-colors: active), where the user's palette replaces the page's. Anywhere else it is a colour no token controls, no theme re-points and no contrast check measures. CSS keywords are case-insensitive, so every spelling counts. stylelint enforces this with design/system-colors-in-forced-colors and the audit as L1 system-color, both in the properties `properties` matches; others are left alone, because `canvas` or `mark` may be a grid-area or an animation name.

sass.about: audit_design alone reads Sass. The stylelint config lints .css files and ships no Sass syntax, and ESLint reads no stylesheet. The audit reads SCSS; indented Sass (.sass) has no braces for it to follow, so it lists each such file as skipped and never passes one.

definitions.rule: A @mixin or @function body emits nothing where it is written, so a rule inside one is not unlayered CSS (Law 5); the layer is checked where the mixin is included. A mixin that holds a whole rule emits it there, so including one at the root of a file is unlayered CSS, directly or through another mixin that includes it; a mixin defined in another file is not followed. An interpolation, #{…}, is text in a selector, a prelude or a value: its braces open and close no rule.
allowed: @layer components { @each $name in (sm, lg) { .card-#{$name} { padding: var(--pad-card); } } .card { color: var(--fg-strong); } }

variables.rule: Law 1: a Sass variable that holds a length, a hex or functional colour, a duration or an easing curve is a literal under another name; a quoted string is text, whatever it spells. It is fixed at compile time, so no theme re-points it, --density cannot reach it and DevTools does not show it. It is refused outside a token file, in a map as in a single value. Two kinds are left alone: a breakpoint ($bp, $bp-*, $breakpoint*), which must be a Sass value because a media query condition cannot read a custom property, and a variable local to a @function, which is a step in a computation.

layers.statement: @layer reset, vendor, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;
layers.rule: Law 5. The entry stylesheet names the layers once, first, in this order: a layer may be left out but never moved, and other layers may sit between them. `theme` is Tailwind v4's generated theme and only a Tailwind entry names it. A layer may hold sub-layers, ordered inside it (`@layer components { @layer base, skin; }`, then `@layer components.skin { … }`): they rank inside their parent and cannot leave it, so the order holds (stack-vanilla-css.md). `vendor` holds CSS you do not control, imported with `layer(vendor)`. The statement names it even before there is any, because a layer first named by its import is appended after `overrides`, where the vendor's rules beat every rule you write (SB-A8). So every layer a file imports into must be in that file's statement, and the statement comes before the import: an `@import … layer(vendor)` above it names `vendor` first, whatever the statement then says. The canonical entries are web-design-studio/assets/starter/styles/index.css, and assets/configs/index.tailwind.css and index.tailwind-v3.css.
layers.imports: A file that opens its own `@layer` block, as every starter file does, is imported bare: `@import url("base.css") layer(base)` nests it as `base.base` (SB-A23). `layer()` is for files that name no layer: vendor CSS and Tailwind's own files.
allowed: @layer reset, vendor, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;
@layer reset, vendor, tokens, theme, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;

@layer reset, vendor, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;
@import url("vendor/datepicker.css") layer(vendor);
refused: @layer reset, tokens, vendor, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;
@layer vendor, reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;

@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;
@import url("vendor/datepicker.css") layer(vendor);

@import url("vendor/datepicker.css") layer(vendor);
@layer reset, vendor, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;

@layer base { body { margin: 0; } }
@layer reset, vendor, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities, overrides;

values.rule: Laws 1, 3 and 6: a design property takes a token through var(), or one of the few values that are not a design decision: 0, the CSS-wide keywords, and the keywords its family lists. stylelint allows exactly these values, property by property (declaration-property-value-allowed-list compares the whole value). The audit reads the same allowlists for the spacing, stroke, motion and sizing families (SPACING_VALUES and the rest), and refuses the literals the other families leave out; a value holding a Sass variable is judged with each reference read as a token, since the audit cannot resolve it (sass.variables): `padding: $space 5%` is refused as `var(--x) 5%` would be. An allowlist names what is correct, so 13px, 0.8125rem and clamp(12px, 2vw, 14px) are refused alike, and so is the spelling nobody has thought of yet.
values.lists: In a family's `values`, KEYWORDS is `keywords`, COLOUR_WORDS is `colour_words` and every system colour (system_colors.names) in any case, and a shape's name stands for its pattern. Every other entry is a value matched exactly.

VAR_SEQ.means: One or more var(--token) references, whitespace-separated, and nothing else but 0, which is on every length scale (zero): `0 var(--pad-card)` is allowed and `var(--pad-card) 2px` is refused. Names are kebab-case: var(--padCard) is a typo, and a var() that names no token drops its declaration in silence.

VAR_ONE.means: Exactly one token, with or without a fallback, which is not checked (var_fallback). For the properties where a sequence means nothing: font-size, z-index, line-height.

VAR_CALC.means: A token plus or minus a token, for the nested-radius rule: inner radius = outer radius - inner padding. No bare number and no factor: calc(var(--space-4) * 1.5) invents a step between steps, Law 3's prohibition inside a calc(). Density scales by multiplying, once, in tokens.css, where it is a system decision.

CANCEL.means: A margin that cancels a known token, Law 2's third exception (margins_in_components). Only -1: any other factor invents a step.

ALIGN.means: A margin that aligns and spaces nothing: one to four 0s and autos. `0 auto` centres, `0 0 0 auto` pushes to the end. A token beside an auto spaces the box, so it is not alignment.

STROKE.means: A border or outline shorthand: tokens (a --stroke-* width, a colour role), 0, a style keyword and the colour words currentColor and transparent, so `1px solid var(--border-default)` and `var(--stroke-default) solid #ddd` are refused. A system colour goes in border-color or outline-color, inside forced-colors (system_colors).

MOTION_LIST.means: A transition or animation shorthand: a comma-separated list of items, each a property or keyframe name and keywords (allow-discrete, infinite, both, none, …), tokens, 0s and an iteration count. Names are lowercase kebab-case, so no spelling of an easing keyword (EASE-IN, Linear) passes as a name. The timing comes from tokens, so a time (200ms), a curve (cubic-bezier(), steps()) and an easing keyword (ease-in, linear) are refused: `translate var(--motion-expand), display var(--motion-expand) allow-discrete` is allowed.

BREAKPOINT.means: A breakpoint in rem, the one literal length a theme binding takes (bindings).

RATIO.means: An aspect ratio such as `16 / 9`, a container format rather than a design value (bindings).

values.colour_functions_rule: A colour written as one of these functions is a literal, unless a token decides it: a function with a var() among its arguments, as in oklch(from var(--x) l c h / 0.5) or color-mix(in oklch, var(--bg-accent) 20%, transparent), is derived. A mix of literals is a literal. A var() fallback is not checked (var_fallback). The audit (raw-color), stylelint (design/no-literal-colour-function, in every property) and ESLint (inline styles) read this list; token files are exempt.

spacing.why: Spacing is the scale or nothing. 0 is on the scale and is spelled 0 (zero), alone or among tokens. gap is the one sanctioned way to space siblings (Law 2), so it takes the scale too, and so does a margin outside a component, in a layout or base file; in a component, margins_in_components holds it to Law 2. A share of the container (calc(100% - var(--gutter-page)), 5%) is not a spacing step: a layout primitive carries it in a socket. `layout` holds examples written in a layout file, where a margin may take a token.

type.why: No em, no %, no bare 1.4: size and leading are the values every project drifts on first. The one em is font-size: 1em, which sizes an icon to the text beside it. line-height takes no literal 1, though --leading-none is 1: the literal teaches the next person that the scale is optional. The font shorthand is how the --type-* roles are read, four values in one declaration that cannot half-apply.

radius.why: 50% is the one exception: a circle is geometry, not a design value, and --radius-full (9999px) makes a pill, not a circle, on a box that is not square.

stroke.why: Line weights are tokens: --stroke-hairline, --stroke-default, --stroke-thick and --stroke-focus are the system's whole set, and forced-colors mode repaints each one. A hand-typed 1px drifts to 1.5px and 3px within a few commits, and thin, medium and thick are the browser's weights, not the system's. A border or outline shorthand takes the tokens, a style keyword and a colour token (STROKE). outline-offset may cancel a token, to draw a ring inside the edge.

elevation.why: Read --elevation-card, not --shadow-sm. A hand-written shadow is one layer and reads as a sticker; the tokens are physically consistent pairs, contact and ambient.

colour.why: currentColor and transparent are keywords, not colours, and the system colours belong to forced-colors mode (system_colors). No hex, no rgb(), no oklch(), not even a temporary one: a literal colour in a component is the one thing dark mode cannot follow.
allowed: background: oklch(from var(--bg-accent) l c h / 0.5)
refused: background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--bg-accent, oklch(50% 0.1 250)) 20%, oklch(98% 0.01 250))

stacking.why: The z-index ladder in tokens.css is closed and ordered by what occupies each rung. z-index: 9999 is not a value but a surrender, and the next person writes 10000.

motion.why: Duration and easing are role-paired in tokens.css: they travel together or they drift. 0s switches one transition off among several. tokens.css collapses every duration token to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion, so a literal 200ms opts the component out: a vestibular-safety failure, not a style nit. An easing keyword (ease-in, linear) is a curve chosen by hand, as cubic-bezier() is. A scroll-driven animation's duration is auto: its timeline owns it.
allowed: transition: opacity var(--motion-enter), display var(--motion-enter) allow-discrete
refused: transition: opacity var(--motion-enter), transform var(--motion-enter) ease-in

sizing.why: Line length is a spacing decision: max-inline-size: 65ch in a component is the same mistake as padding: 13px, and the one people defend hardest. So are the sizes of things: a box takes a token (--tap-min, a measure, a socket), 100%, auto or an intrinsic keyword, and 1em sizes an icon to its text. The page shell may use the small and dynamic viewport units in the block axis: 100svb does not jump when mobile browser chrome hides. A size derived from tokens, calc(100% - var(--gutter-page) * 2), is geometry: it goes in a socket the property reads, as the starter's layout.css does.

inline_styles.rule: Law 4: the style prop is a second home for a component's styles, where no stylesheet, theme, media query or audit reaches. Its one legal use passes a value only the runtime knows into CSS as a custom property; a design literal there is Law 1 coming back through that exception. A design literal is a string holding a number with one of `literal_units`, a hex, or a colour function (values.colour_functions).

bindings.rule: A theme file (file_classes.binding_files, Tailwind v4's theme.css) binds Tailwind's theme to the tokens and decides nothing (theme.css §0): a custom property there takes a token, currentColor, transparent or a CSS-wide keyword. Each prefix with a rule of its own answers to that rule alone, so the colour words never reach a breakpoint, a ratio or an animation. Two literals are allowed, each because of CSS: a breakpoint in rem, which must be a literal and never a var(), because a media query condition cannot read a custom property, and an aspect ratio, a container format. A breakpoint may also be a CSS-wide keyword: `--breakpoint-*: initial` clears Tailwind's own, and `--breakpoint-2xl: initial` one of them. An --animate-* binding is an animation shorthand, so it takes the motion tokens (MOTION_LIST). Keyframe geometry, §0's third exception, is not a custom property. Only custom properties are held to this: the theme file's other rules (its @utility blocks, its keyframes) answer to the gates' other rules. stylelint's theme-file override reads BINDING_ALLOWLIST, and the audit, for which a theme file is a token file, checks its custom properties against BINDING_VALUES (L1 binding-literal).

binding_files.about: Theme files bind a framework's theme to the tokens (bindings). Each is also a token file: the audit and the migration tool leave its literals to this rule.
